blocks.h2: Signs Your Water Heater Needs Repair

tiles.body: A pilot, igniter, element or valve that failed.
Sediment or a failing burner or element.
Valve leaks can be fixed. Tank leaks can't.
Often a venting or safety switch problem.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Problems in Lincoln Park Homes
blocks.intro: Water heaters here live in basements, utility closets and tight mechanical rooms.

items.body: A leak inside a unit can reach the neighbor below. We check pans and drains.
In older buildings, gas heaters may vent into a chimney shared with other appliances.
Many condos have electric heaters, with elements and thermostats that fail.
Narrow stairs and tight closets take planning.

bodies: We repair gas and electric tank heaters, power-vent units and tankless heaters in Lincoln Park houses, two-flats and condos.
When you call, read us the label: fuel, size and date. If it's time to replace it, see [water heater installation](/chicago-lincoln-park/water-heater-installation).
A yearly flush clears sediment and helps the heater last. We also test the relief valve, check the anode rod and inspect the burner or elements and the venting.
Tankless heaters need descaling on a schedule.

blocks.h2: Water Heaters in Lincoln Park Condos
blocks.body: Many condo units have their own water heater in a closet, often on an upper floor. That location means a small leak can become a big problem for the unit below. If you see water around the base, shut off the cold supply at the top of the heater and call us. We'll tell you whether it's a valve we can replace or a tank that's failed, and we'll plan the replacement around your building's rules.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: My condo heater is leaking. What should I do?
items.preview: Shut off the water to the heater and call us.
items.answer: Close the cold water valve on top of the heater and turn off its power or gas. Then call us. If water is reaching the unit below, let your neighbor know.

items.q: Is it worth repairing an older heater?
items.preview: Under 8 years, usually. Over 12, usually not.
items.answer: If it's under about 8 years and a part failed, usually yes. Past 12 years or if the tank leaks, replacement is the better value.

items.q: Do you service electric water heaters?
items.answer: Yes. We replace elements, thermostats and the rest of the parts on electric heaters.

items.q: How long do water heaters last?
items.answer: Tank heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years.

items.q: Do I need to tell my association about a new heater?
items.answer: Some associations require notice or a permit. Check your rules.

items.q: How much does water heater repair cost in Lincoln Park?
items.preview: It depends on the part and the heater. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what failed and the type of heater. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
